compliance: On the UK Xylella medium-risk host list; trade sales of plants for growing-on need a plant passport.
cvs: 'Brown Turkey' – hardiest, most reliable outdoors · 'Brunswick' – large green-yellow fruit · 'White Marseilles' – pale green fruit · 'Rouge de Bordeaux' – best under glass
foliage: deciduous; large, rough, deeply three- to five-lobed leaves
hardinessNote: Hardy in most of the UK in an average winter, approximately -10 to -5°C; may need winter protection in cold areas.
pollination: self-fertile; UK-grown varieties set fruit without pollination
prune: Late winter: remove dead, crossing and frost-damaged wood. Early summer: pinch new shoots to five leaves. Late autumn: remove larger unripe figs.
resilience: Drought tolerant once established and good in heat against a warm wall; hard frosts kill back young growth. Pests: scale insect, red spider mite under glass, birds and wasps on fruit, coral spot.
soilWarning: Restrict roots or it grows leaf, not fruit
toxicity: Milky sap is a skin irritant and can cause blistering rashes in sunlight; wear gloves when pruning. Chewed leaves can irritate the mouth and stomach of dogs and cats.
uncertain: size: RHS 2.5–4 m; worldplants 3–6 m; wall-trained or pot-grown plants stay smaller
hardiness: RHS H4, notes winter protection may be needed

compliance: Defra lists Ficus carica as a Xylella medium-risk host; passport enforced only when marketed for growing-on (Plant Health Portal page, date not confirmed); list being updated by 31 Jan 2026 with fig carried over
toxicity: sap phototoxicity and pet irritation from general sources; word edible kept out so the card shows the amber sap warning
peak: main outdoor UK crop Aug-Sep
uses: Warm walls · patio containers · Mediterranean gardens · fruit · conservatories
visual: Edible purple-brown to green figs late summer · bold, deeply lobed tropical-looking leaves · grey bark
water: Water pots generously while fruit swells; established plants in the ground need water only in long dry spells.
